name: Equation
description: You are given an equation: Ax 2 + Bx + C = 0 . Your task is to find the number of distinct roots of the equation and print all of them in ascending order.
input_specification: The first line contains three integer numbers A , B and C ( - 10 5 ≤ A , B , C ≤ 10 5 ). Any coefficient may be equal to 0.
output_specification: In case of infinite root count print the only integer -1 . In case of no roots print the only integer 0 . In other cases print the number of root on the first line and the roots on the following lines in the ascending order. Print roots with at least 5 digits after the decimal point.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 20B — Equation [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
